🔥 बॉलीवुड के महानायक के फैंस के लिए आई है एक बहुत बड़ी खबर!

दिल्ली High Court ने अमिताभ बच्चन के पर्सनालिटी राइट्स मामले में सुनवाई करते हुए उनके पक्ष में फाइनल फैसला सुना दिया है। 👨‍⚖️

कोर्ट के आदेश के मुताबिक अब बिना इजाजत बिग बी के नाम, फोटो, आवाज या पहचान का कमर्शियल इस्तेमाल पूरी तरह बैन रहेगा। पहले उनकी सहमति के बिना फर्जी KBC लॉटरी मैसेज, वीडियो कॉल app, क्विज बुक, T-shirts, posters और domain name amitabhbachchan.in का इस्तेमाल किया जा रहा था। 📱

मामले में Rajat Nagi, Manoj Publications, Tamatina और Mahesh Patel नाम के चार डिफेंडेंट्स ने समझौता कर लिया है और ऐप डिलीट करने व पोस्टर-बुक की बिक्री रोकने पर सहमति जताई है। 📜

अदालत ने पहचान न हो सकने वाले अज्ञात लोगों यानी John Does और कोर्ट में पेश न होने वाले बाकी आरोपियों पर भी यह फैसला लागू किया है।

क्या आपको लगता है कि बॉलीवुड के बाकी स्टार्स को भी अपनी पहचान सुरक्षित रखने के लिए ऐसे ही कोर्ट जाना चाहिए? कमेंट्स में अपनी राय जरूर बताएं! 👇

ctx.text:
The Delhi High Court has passed a final decree in favour of Amitabh Bachchan in his personality rights case, restraining several entities and unidentified persons from commercially using his name, image, voice or likeness without his consent. The order was passed by Justice Purushaindra Kumar Kaurav, concluding proceedings that began with an interim injunction in November 2022.
The Court held that the right to control the commercial use of an individual's identity falls under the “right to publicity”. It observed that Bachchan's name and photographs had been used without permission in ways that could falsely suggest his endorsement of products or services.
The actor had approached the Court over the alleged unauthorised use of his identity across different platforms and merchandise. These included a mobile application titled Amitabh Bachchan Video Call, messages promoting a purported Kaun Banega Crorepati lottery, a general knowledge quiz book featuring his photograph, T-shirts, posters and domain names incorporating his identity.
The Court noted that the unauthorised use involved Bachchan's “very name and photographs” and found that the requirements for protecting his publicity rights had been met.
The final decree also covers unidentified individuals, commonly referred to as John Does. The Court took note of the continued use of Bachchan's persona through anonymous websites, applications, posters and messaging platforms, observing that those responsible may not always be identifiable.
Four defendants, Rajat Nagi, Manoj Publications, Tamatina and Mahesh Patel, settled the matter with Bachchan and acknowledged his publicity and privacy rights. As part of the settlement, the defendants agreed to discontinue the use of his identity. The commitments included deleting the video-call application, stopping publication of the quiz book and sale of posters, and deleting the domain name amitabhbachchan.in.
The remaining defendants did not appear before the Court or file written statements despite being served. The Court held that the case did not involve disputed facts requiring a trial and granted a summary judgment against them. It also clarified that Bachchan could initiate fresh proceedings if further unauthorised use of his persona occurs.
The November 2022 interim injunction now stands merged with the final decree.
